distinct_convention_note: The ProofWiki source explicitly provides the Kuratowski realization. It is a rigorous implementation of ordered coordinates in ZF-style set theory. Alternative Wiener or empty-set-based encodings can satisfy the same pair equality criterion but are not literally the same set.

ProofWiki's subset page gives the universal membership criterion and uses non-strict ⊆. The separate strict variant requires inequality; treating ⊆ as universally strict would be mathematically incorrect and conflict with common conventions.

This stricter relation is sourced from the independently examined subset/proper-subset distinction. Unlike the ordinary subset relation, proper subset never permits A=B; it is not a second meaning for the same non-strict symbol.

ProofWiki Mapping Definition 1 is total and single-valued. This pedagogically earlier element-assignment formulation keeps X as the full domain, Y as the specified codomain, and excludes partial or multivalued assignments.

ProofWiki Mapping Definition 2 gives a typed relation and the two conditions existence and uniqueness. This form is equivalent to total single-valued assignment when domains and codomains are fixed but differs as an object from a bare subset.

This source-dependent bare-subset representation is valid only with specified ambient X and Y and a totality/uniqueness condition. It must not be identified as literally the same typed object as (X,Y,G), especially when distinct codomains contain the same image.
